desc:
App Store listing optimization for iOS apps is the work of making your app page clear, accurate and easy to find. Ecom Swift LLC rewrites your title, subtitle, keywords, description and screenshots in App Store Connect, and trims your app's launch time too.

## What is App Store listing optimization?

App Store listing optimization, often called ASO, is the process of improving the words and images on your app's product page so the right people find the app and understand it quickly. It covers the title, subtitle, keyword field, description, promotional text, screenshots, preview video and the update notes.

It is not a trick. It is careful writing and design that follows Apple's metadata rules and describes the app honestly.

## Why the listing matters as much as the app

Most visitors never open your app before judging it. They read two lines and glance at the first few screenshots, then decide. If the page does not explain the benefit in that moment, a good app goes unnoticed.

Search works the same way. People type a phrase into the App Store search box, and the store matches it against your title, subtitle and keyword field. Words that are missing from those fields are words your app is less likely to be found for.

## How a better listing changes results

A stronger listing improves two steps: being found and being chosen. Better keywords and a clearer title help the app appear for phrases real people search for. A clear subtitle and screenshots with short captions help the visitor see the point at once, and tap Get.

We cannot promise a particular ranking. Ranking depends on competition, ratings, downloads and many things Apple does not publish. What we can do is remove avoidable weaknesses on the page you control.

## Launch time, the quiet part of conversion

A slow first launch costs you users before they see anything. If the app shows a blank screen while it loads data, many people will assume it is broken. We measure how long your app takes to open and look for the largest delays, such as heavy work on startup, large images and network calls that block the first screen.

Fixing those delays helps new users reach the first useful screen sooner, which the listing can then promise honestly.

## What a strong App Store listing includes

- A title that names the app and one clear benefit, within Apple's character limit.
- A subtitle that adds a second search phrase and says what the app does.
- A keyword field filled without repeats, plurals or words already in the title.
- A description whose first lines explain the value before the Read More cut.
- Promotional text that you can update without a new app version.
- Screenshots with short captions that tell a story from first screen to last.
- Correct category and age rating, based on what the app really contains.
- An app preview video plan, when a short demo helps.
- Update notes that tell returning users what changed.

## How we work

We read your current page, look at the apps people compare yours to and decide how to describe yours in plain words. Then we write options for the title and subtitle, build the keyword field and rewrite the description. For screenshots we use real screens from your app and add captions that fit the device frame.

Basic covers the text fields and a short launch-time report. Standard adds full listing copy, new screenshots and a few launch-time fixes. Premium adds screenshots for two device sizes, a video storyboard, two translations and a larger round of launch fixes. Everything is prepared in App Store Connect under your account, and you press publish.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Describe what the app does in the first sentence of the description.
- Use screenshots that show real screens from the current version.
- Write for the person searching, not for the search engine.
- Update the promotional text when you run a sale or add a feature.
- Check that your claims match what the app actually does.

**Avoid:**
- Putting competitor names or trademarks in the keyword field.
- Repeating the same word in the title, subtitle and keywords.
- Claiming chart positions, honors or prices that may change.
- Using mock-ups that show features the app does not have.
- Changing the whole listing every week, which makes results hard to read.

## Who this is for

This service fits a developer who built a good app and wrote the listing in a hurry. It suits an owner whose downloads are flat despite steady traffic, and a team about to release an update that wants fresh screenshots and notes. It also helps an app that is not live yet, since the first listing sets the tone.

## What we need from you

Send us a short note about your app and its audience, the current store link or a TestFlight build, and your brand assets. For App Store Connect we work as a team member with a limited role such as Marketing, and we never need your password or Apple ID login. For the launch-time work, we also need access to the code through a repository invitation.
